app.title: Codebook reconciler for two coders
app.summary: Two people who coded the same excerpts independently open the page to see how far they agree: percent agreement and Cohen's kappa overall, and a table of counts and kappa for each code. They then work through a queue of the excerpts they coded differently, each shown with both coders' codes and definitions side by side, and settle it by taking one coder's code or another code with a short note, while a progress bar counts what is resolved. When a definition caused the disagreement they edit it in place, with the original wording and a log of every change kept. The final code for every excerpt exports as CSV, and the revised codebook with the agreement statistics exports as JSON.

task.text: Measure agreement between two independent coders and resolve their disagreements one excerpt at a time, revising code definitions where the codebook caused them.

data.text: Interview excerpts, each coded once by each of two coders with a single code from a shared codebook of named codes with definitions, plus the resolutions, notes and definition changes made while reconciling.
data.item: an interview excerpt with one code from each of two coders

stage.text: checking inter-rater reliability and merging two coders' work

mechanism.text: A summary bar shows overall agreement and resolution progress; a left column holds a per-code agreement table above the disagreement queue, and the right pane shows the current disagreement with both coders' choices side by side. Clicking a code's row filters the queue to disagreements involving it, keys step through the queue and take either coder's code, and each resolution moves on to the next open item.

field.text: qualitative interview coding in CSCW and health informatics

workflow.name: measure agreement between two labellers and resolve their disagreements

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The page computes percent agreement and Cohen's kappa over all excerpts and codes, and a kappa per code treating it as present or absent, each with its strength band; per-code kappas below 0.6 are in bold.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Clicking a code's row in the agreement table narrows the disagreement queue to excerpts where either coder used that code, with how many of them are resolved.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: The queue lists only the excerpts the two coders coded differently, each marked open or resolved; j and k move through it and each decision jumps to the next open one.

steps.step: find where people disagree and resolve it
steps.here: The excerpt is shown above coder A's and coder B's code and definition side by side; 1 or 2 takes one coder's code, a menu offers any other code, a note records why, and Reopen takes a decision back.

steps.step: revise a category's definition and log the change
steps.here: The definitions of the two codes in question can be rewritten beside the excerpt; the original wording stays shown and each edit is logged with its old and new text and the excerpt being discussed.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: A bar in the summary counts disagreements resolved out of all of them, and a filtered queue shows its own resolved count.

A CSV gives the final code for every excerpt, agreed ones keeping their shared code and open ones blank, with both coders' codes and the note; a JSON file holds the codebook with original and edited definitions, the change log and the agreement statistics.

distinctive: Each excerpt has exactly one code from each of two coders, so every disagreement is a pair of codes, settled as either coder's code or a third one.
Agreement is Cohen's kappa computed in the page, overall and per code, with Landis and Koch bands; it describes the independent coding and does not change as disagreements are resolved.
The per-code agreement table doubles as the queue's filter, so the codes the coders understand differently are worked through together.
Definitions are edited during reconciliation with the original wording kept and every change logged against an excerpt, so the methods memo can say what changed and why.
Exports are shaped for a methods appendix: a final code for every excerpt, and the revised codebook with the agreement statistics.
